schema.title: IUIDocument
schema.description: The project-defined iui/1 wire contract. Semantic validation additionally enforces safe expressions, data and URLs. Native nodes are recognized but unsupported by the portable renderer.

contracts.text:
## 状态与表达式

`state` 保存字符串、有限数值或布尔值。引用写作 `{ "$": "gain" }`，计算写作 `{ "op": "mul", "args": [12, { "$": "gain" }] }`。

可用操作符：`add`、`sub`、`mul`、`div`、`max`、`min`、`round`、`abs`、`clamp`、`gt`、`lt`、`eq`、`if`、`format`。它们是受约束的数据树，不是 JavaScript 源码。未知引用、循环依赖、非法参数、除零及非有限结果会被拒绝。

需要直接求值时，可从主入口导入 `evaluateValue` 和 `evaluateState`；通常由控件与渲染器自动处理即可。

# API and security model

`iui/1` is data, never executable source. Content text is inserted through text nodes. The only HTML sink is KaTeX's generated visual HTML plus accessible MathML with `trust:false`, bounded expansion/size, and strict parsing; model HTML never enters that sink directly. Unsupported TeX falls back to visible source.

## Validation

The JSON Schema is generated from `scripts/generate-schema.mjs`. TypeScript declarations and the Ajv standalone validator are generated in the same step. CI rejects drift. Browser code imports the already generated validator, avoiding runtime `new Function` and allowing a script hash CSP without `unsafe-eval`.

`validateDocument(input)` returns `{ok:true,document}` or `{ok:false,issues}`. It accepts plain JSON values only; custom prototypes, accessors, cyclic objects, reserved keys, nonfinite numbers, and excessive values/text/depth are rejected before Ajv traversal. Semantics additionally reject unknown references, computed cycles, bad operator arities/types, numerical errors, duplicate IDs, unknown state bindings, broken topology endpoints, malformed table widths, invalid chart data, and unsafe resource declarations.

`evaluateValue(value,state,computed)` evaluates a constrained expression and throws on invalid input. `evaluateState(document,override)` returns validated, frozen state/computed results or issues. Controller state updates use this checked path. Numeric operators do not coerce strings. `if` is lazy at evaluation but both branches are inspected for references and types; runtime arithmetic errors still reject the state transition.

Limits include 64 JSON nesting levels, 2,000 node-like objects, 50,000 values, a two-million-UTF-16-code-unit text budget (including JSON keys, retained across merged state updates), and schema-specific row/series/child limits. These limits reduce resource exhaustion; they are not a promise of fixed latency for every valid document.

## Browser boundary

No raw HTML, CSS, JS, callback, import, network action, form submission, or arbitrary AppBlock is accepted. SVG uses a fixed shape list and numeric/color/geometry attribute allowlists. `native` is recognized solely to report `UNSUPPORTED_NATIVE`. It does not load an adapter.

Model URLs are limited to the documented link/image policy. Remote images require a reader action and use no-referrer. URLs still lead to third parties when a reader activates them; validation does not certify the destination's content or privacy. Callers handling confidential documents should avoid remote URLs altogether.

Compiled inline HTML applies a CSP containing the exact SHA-256 of its runtime. It blocks network connections, objects, forms, base URL changes, and remote scripts/fonts; font-src data: permits the bundled official WOFF2 fonts. Styles allow inline rules because the renderer writes bounded, host-owned numeric/enum properties. The host browser's CSP remains authoritative for `mount`; pass `styles:false` and serve the stylesheet when embedding under a stricter host policy.

`compileHtml(input,{assets:'inline',backend:'portable',lang})` emits one self-contained HTML file. `compileArtifact(input,{assets:'shared',assetBase:'./iui-assets/',lang})` also returns an asset map with safe relative file paths. Shared output is intended for a static HTTP server; no claim is made for every browser's file-origin shared-script policy. Both reject unsupported backends.

## Lifecycle and scope

Controllers isolate state. `update` validates the complete next document and resets state. `setState` merges a scalar patch, verifies all bindings and derived values, then updates existing nodes without replacing focused controls. `dispose` is idempotent and removes its owned elements, listeners, and resize observer. External DOM edits by the embedding host are outside this contract.

The library does not authenticate users, persist documents, store credentials, run simulations as scientific truth, fetch sources, or verify model-generated facts. Applications remain responsible for provenance, permissions, and their host threat model.

JSON Schema string `maxLength` and evaluated Value/state string maxima use Unicode code points. A Value string accepts at most 12,000 code points, including astral characters, while the independent whole-document resource budget still counts UTF-16 storage units. The resolved evaluation context (state, computed scalars and the evaluated Value) is checked against the same storage budget before DOM creation or refresh; accepted documents therefore do not defer that rejection until rendering. Native form minLength/maxLength constraints retain HTML UTF-16 semantics; they do not redefine the global string contract.

# Supplied legacy category review and river puzzle

These are two separate complete local contracts. The legacy view does not alter financial records or contact an account service. The puzzle implements the classic three-item rules locally; its follow-up requests do not start a conversation.

## Legacy category correction

`ledger-low-confidence-category-correction-legacy` has a supplied title, account-availability flag, empty text and up to100 uniquely identified transactions. Each transaction keeps its exact name, date, amount/category labels and correction query. `amountValue` only supplies the sign for positive presentation; it never rewrites the amount label. A null or omitted sign is neutral. Masking uses each supplied masked amount label and neutralizes the sign tone.

The initial list has three records. More/Less switches three/all while retaining record and media DOM identity. Hidden rows cannot dispatch requests. On collapse/reset, keyboard focus inside a newly hidden row returns to More. Empty data displays the supplied empty text. `connected:false` renders only a supplied `noAccounts` title/description/action label and finite query, not the hidden transaction list or opaque host action JSON.

Row activation requests `correct-category` with the transaction ID, exact query and title. Onboarding requests its supplied query. There is no implicit mutation, generated category, connector identifier or host system hint. Images are supplied: inline media can load immediately; external logos require an explicit sibling control outside the row's action button. Loading restores focus to the row action, and update/disposal releases media URLs. Missing logos use an original supplied glyph; source failure follows the existing image hide-on-failure contract.

## SuperbowlRiddle

`superbowl-riddle` is the finite fox/chicken/grain river-crossing puzzle. All display instructions, item/bank/boat labels, terminal messages and follow-up prompts are supplied. No reference artwork or follow-up prose is bundled. An optional initial snapshot places each of the three items exactly once across two banks and at most one cargo slot. Boat side and supplied initial outcome are explicit.

Only the current bank can be picked from. Selecting another item swaps current cargo back onto that bank. Unload returns cargo to the current bank. Cross checks the bank being left unattended: chicken with fox or grain loses. Cargo is automatically delivered on the other bank; all three safely on the right wins. Empty-boat crossings are allowed. Terminal states disable/hide game actions and expose only the appropriate supplied follow-ups plus Reset.

Reset always returns to the canonical all-left, empty-cargo, left-boat, playing arrangement, even when the initial supplied snapshot was different. This follows the observed puzzle contract. Native reset has the same target but honors cancellation and newer accepted game input. Keyboard activation uses real buttons; moving a focused item into/out of cargo restores focus to its new meaningful control. A terminal crossing restores focus to Reset.

## Requests and lifetime

`iui:supplied-interaction` details are frozen, bubbling, cancelable and non-composed. Supported intents are category/onboarding, disclosure, puzzle pick/unload/cross/reset and follow-up. Game intents expose a separately frozen proposed `next` snapshot, including frozen bank arrays. Canceling a request leaves local state unchanged. Acceptance applies only local presentation/game state or records a receipt.

A stable visible Reset anchors native form handling. Source disabled, fieldset/first-legend, ARIA, hidden/inert and capture cancellation remain effective after DOM-property tampering. Shared intent admission and generation ownership protect constructor recursion, update/disposal and same-turn ancestor removal. New local disclosure/game input can supersede a queued native reset; external-style category/follow-up requests wait until the pending reset settles.

Author DOM/compiler checks, native test discovery, independent consumers and actual browser/pixel acceptance remain separate. The distributed/native-validated unified183 assets are unchanged by this source candidate.

Accepted game reset moves focus to the visible Reset button only when the currently focused cargo, terminal action or bank item will become hidden. Cancelled reset and a newer game input retain focus and state. Existing pick/unload/cross focus destinations still take precedence. This is a local focus correction; the shared reset contract is unchanged.

## Complete semantic validation boundary

Full `validateDocument` requires a nonblank top-level label (`INTERACTION_TEXT`). In the legacy category-correction card, title and every direct transaction string except `logoAlt` must be nonblank; transaction IDs must be unique (`INTERACTION_ID`), and logos safe images. A disconnected (`connected:false`) card requires its supplied no-account view (`INTERACTION_NO_ACCOUNTS`). This preserves the existing limited check rather than adding a blanket trim rule to every top-level content field.

For the finite river puzzle, every supplied `labels` value is nonblank. Won and lost follow-up IDs must each be nonblank and unique within their list; this validator does not add a new trim rule to follow-up label/query beyond their structural bounds. If an initial snapshot is supplied, fox, chicken and grain must each occur exactly once across left bank, right bank and cargo (`RIDDLE_SNAPSHOT`). The local state machine remains unchanged; no inference about external activities is made.
